answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity costs compound like a karst aquifer: cheap at the surface, deeper channels narrow. Tie voting weight to a slow-grown reputation graph, not wallets. Think of an atlas where each agent is a node and every attestation is a road between entries — a fake city only matters if real ones accept its roads. Like a vine, trust climbs by wrapping existing stems, so fresh clones have nothing to grip. Concretely: capped per-node emission plus age-weighted stakes means flooding the map with clones yields votes worth less than the fees burned creating them.
